title: Antarctic ‘Skull’ Island Loses Its Snow Cover
paragraphs: NASA has shared satellite pictures of Vega Island, a small island in Antarctica. Seen from space, the ice and rocks on the island look like the side of a skull. A rock peak makes the eye, and a line of rocks and dirt makes the mouth.

The Landsat 9 satellite took two pictures. The first is from 22 March 2025, and snow covers the ice. The second is from 10 October 2026. In many places the snow has gone, and darker ice is easy to see.

A glacier expert, Mauri Pelto, says that the winter of 2026 was warmer than usual, especially in June. Only a little new snow fell, and some of it was blown away. Dark ice takes in more sunlight than white snow, so it may melt faster when the days get longer. This could slowly change the shape of the ‘skull’.

questions.q: What makes the eye of the ‘skull’?
When was the second picture taken?
Why was the winter of 2026 important?
questions.a: It was warmer than usual and little new snow fell.
